learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Almost never and locked the predicted frequency of six or fewer correct answers on ten fresh cases for a model truly correct 80% of the time.
observations.exploration: Ran one ten-case test, then 100 more. Among 101 tests, nine scored 60% or less and the spread was ±12.4 points. Switched to 1,000 cases, automatically producing 100 tests with zero low scores and ±1.2 points spread. Switched to 100 cases: 100 tests, zero low scores, ±4.0 points spread.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to about one in eight, accurately quoted nine of 101 small tests, and distinguished that 9% sample frequency from the exact 12.1% chance. It accurately recalled the 1,000 case spread despite the current 100 case state, then explained the inverse square root sample size relationship.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot after 101 ten-case tests. A histogram spread across scores from 50% to 100%, with low-score bins colored red and an 80% reference. Sample size, count and spread readouts were legible.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The prompt challenges overconfidence in a small evaluation score.
prediction.evidence: Selected almost never for a 60% observed score from an 80% model.

interaction.reason: Repeated tests and sample size changes isolate sampling noise.
interaction.evidence: Spread fell from 12.4 points at ten cases to 4.0 at 100 and 1.2 at 1,000.

payoff.reason: The reveal carefully separates sample frequency, exact probability and typical spread.
payoff.evidence: It quotes 9 of 101 versus exact 12.1% and the observed larger test spread.

clarity.reason: The histogram and explicit sample size make variability inspectable.
clarity.evidence: Low-score bins are visually separated from the full distribution.

transfer.reason: A general evaluation principle is explained without a new application.
transfer.evidence: The lesson stays with the fixed 80% model and held-out test cases.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: A genuinely 80% model can often look like a 60% model on ten cases.
surprise.evidence: Nine of 101 sampled small tests scored 60% or less.

visualExplanation.reason: The distribution reveals what a single score conceals.
visualExplanation.evidence: The broad ten-case histogram supports the noise explanation.

playfulness.reason: Repeated random tests invite investigation but remain analytic.
playfulness.evidence: One-test and hundred-test buttons build a distribution.

practicalValue.reason: It discourages treating tiny benchmark scores as precise ability estimates.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal states more held-out cases reduce measurement noise.

depth.reason: The lesson includes finite sample variation and a quantitative scaling rule.
depth.evidence: Observed frequency differs from exact chance, and spread follows 1 over square root n.

complexity.reason: Frequency and histogram reasoning are approachable, while spread and square root scaling add statistical concepts.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: distinguish true accuracy, one observed score and a distribution of repeated scores.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: two sampling buttons and three sample size choices.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: The model can remain unchanged while observed evaluation results vary substantially.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Sampling uncertainty and spread scaling are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate: percentages, histogram bins, ± points and 1/√n notation.

whyCool: Repeating the same evaluation turns an apparently definitive score into a visibly noisy measurement.
caveat: The model has a fixed independent 80% success probability; real dataset dependence or distribution shifts are not explored.
missingEvidence: No fresh true accuracy or different application was tested.
